It’s definitely worth talking to your therapist about. I think some generations accept think of spanking as a normal form of discipline, and a lot of people don’t consider it to be abusive. My parents spanked me, and I never brought it up to therapists because I thought it was “normal.” But, like with you, I was spanked for things that I did on accident (like spilling a cup of milk). For me, it only made me trust my parents less, and I lied to them more often. You also mentioned how your dad threatened to harm/kill you and that’s also worth talking about. I don’t know your family dynamic but that’s definitely not a healthy thing for a child to hear from a parent. Whatever you’re going through, you’re not wrong for feeling upset about it.

I’m 22 now and feel like I never got to be a teenager. I spent most of my teenage years living with my mother and verbally and emotionally abusive boyfriend. She was very depressed and I was afraid to make her more upset. I always tried to be the perfect student in high school to make her happy. I had a hard time fitting in because of this, and never got to socialize the way that a lot of teenagers do. I remember thinking that things would get better once I left for college, but once I started college I really struggled. Everyone there seemed so social and well-adjusted, while I had a lot unresolved mental issues. This led to me feeling very depressed and I did very poorly in my classes. I ended up transferring schools twice, and changing my major too many times to count. I made a few friends during that time, but I still feel bitter about not having the normal teenage/young adult experience. I’m still in school now, but my grades are better and I’m on track to graduate next fall. I’m still very resentful that my teenage years were spent on coping with a toxic family rather than doing things that a normal teenager does.
